51441622.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human HSP90-alpha N-terminal domain assessed as change in enthalpy by measuring dissociation constant at 100 uM at 25 degC by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Thermodynamic Analysis of the Binding of THS-510 to Human Hsp90α NTD. Thermodynamic parameters for the interaction of the ligand and human Hsp90α NTD were determined using a MicroCal iTC200 isothermal titration calorimetry instrument (Malvern Instruments). The compound solution (100 μM) was titrated into a sample cell containing a solution of human Hsp90α NTD (10 μM). These experiments were conducted in 150 mM NaCl, 20 mM Tris-HCl, 5% DMSO, pH 7.5 at a constant temperature over the range of 15–30 °C. The free energy of ligand binding is described by the following equation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. The heat capacity upon binding was derived from ITC experiments at different temperatures: ΔCp = d(ΔH)/dT.
original_paragraph.Competitive Isothermal Binding Analysis: Competitive titration analysis was performed by titrating ligand (600 μM) into the sample cell containing human Hsp90α NTD (20 μM) and a known Hsp90 inhibitor (100 μM) at 25 °C.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Characteristics of the interaction of THS-975 and THS-510 with Hsp90. (a, d) Chemical structure of THS-975 and THS-510. (b, e) Isoform selectivity of THS-975 and THS-510. Plotted is the percent ratio of the intensity of the test and control lines versus concentration of inhibitor. The data are the means of two independent experiments. (c, f) Enthalpy change on the binding of THS-975 and THS-510 to the human Hsp90α NTD.
original_paragraph.Results section (page 2672): As shown in Figure 3f, moderate binding of THS-510 to HSP90 was observed (KD = 2.7 μM) at 25 °C. The stoichiometry of binding calculated for THS-510 from the ITC data was 0.72 ± 0.03; therefore, THS-510 likely binds human Hsp90α in a 1:1 molar ratio. The thermodynamic parameters of the interaction between THS-510 and human Hsp90α NTD were ΔG of −7.6 ± 0.1 kcal/mol, ΔH of −5.7 ± 0.2 kcal/mol, and −TΔS of −1.9 ± 0.1 kcal/mol, indicating that complex formation was primarily enthalpy driven.
original_paragraph.Thermodynamic Characterization of TAS-11: To characterize the molecular mechanisms of the binding of THS-510 and TAS-116 to Hsp90, we examined the heat capacity changes (ΔCp) over the temperature range from 20 to 30 °C using ITC (Figure 5b, Figure S6). Unexpectedly, binding of THS-510 to the human Hsp90α NTD had a positive ΔCp value (0.56 kcal/mol·K), whereas that of TAS-116 had a negative ΔCp value (−0.29 kcal/mol·K).
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Figure 5. (a) Thermodynamic parameters for the interactions of THS-510, THS-762, and TAS-116 with human Hsp90α NTD. (b) Temperature dependence of the binding enthalpy change for THS-510 and TAS-116 binding to the human Hsp90α NTD. (c) Chemical structure of THS-762 and predicted regions of Hsp90 bound by each part of the molecule.
